policy_note: The oracle checks a bounded delivery-feasibility chain. It does not perform routing, inventory allocation, procurement, dispatch, vehicle certification, lift planning, custody approval or building installation. All values are synthetic.

semantics.time: Integer ticks; delivery windows and site gate windows are half-open [start,end). Acceptance exactly at end is Late.
semantics.inventory: Physical lot quantity is owner-declared; allocations across all candidate deliveries are summed. Over-allocation blocks all affected candidates; no order-dependent first-come allocation is invented.
semantics.qualification: Product, grade, design revision and BOM digest must match the exact use. Revoked, wrong-grade or failed inspection evidence is Rejected.
semantics.route: Route, vehicle and payload are owner-evidence inputs. This oracle does not compute a route or infer legal vehicle access.
semantics.resources: Receiving-bay and laydown uses are summed by resource and slot. Capacity overbooking blocks all contenders; no schedule/dispatch is generated.
semantics.receipt: DeliveryFeasible means inputs support a planned delivery; AcceptedDelivery additionally requires full quantity received, custody accepted and independent inspection passed.
semantics.origin: Imported source may be deliverable, but the adapter always sets local_productive_capability_claim=false. It does not prove local manufacture.

cases.description: Qualified lot, correct grade, route and receiving path; delivery is already accepted.
Qualification evidence is unknown; the lot cannot be called qualified.
Product family exists but technical grade is wrong.
Declared source inventory is below the work-package demand.
Two deliveries together over-allocate one shared material lot.
Production completes after the latest site acceptance time.
Vehicle payload capacity is below the declared load mass.
Vehicle volume capacity is below the declared load volume.
Vehicle is prohibited by the declared route restriction.
Route evidence is stale; transport feasibility is unknown.
Travel plus unload and inspection duration cannot fit the delivery window.
Site gate is known to be closed.
Site gate status is unknown.
Unloading equipment is unavailable.
Unloading equipment capacity is insufficient for the load.
Laydown resource capacity is below the required staging footprint.
Receiving labour is unavailable in the booked window.
Independent receiving inspection failed.
All delivery conditions are feasible but receiving inspection is still pending.
Only part of the planned quantity has been received.
The physical receipt is disputed; it must not be accepted.
Material lot qualification has been revoked.
Two deliveries contend for one receiving bay in the same time slot.
Route origin is withheld; no transport pass can be established.
Imported supply is deliverable, but the adapter must not claim local productive capability.
The construction BOM revision changed after procurement; the lot no longer matches.
Acceptance would complete exactly at the half-open delivery-window endpoint.
Source and demand use incompatible quantity units; the comparison is unsupported.
Duplicate delivery identifiers make the entire comparison unsupported.
A delivery from a different evaluation scope cannot be compared.
Inventory record is stale; declared stock is not usable evidence.
The custody receipt exists but has been revoked.
Two deliveries exceed shared laydown capacity; neither can claim the same space.
